name: org.machanism.machai:project-layout
description: Project Layout is a Java 8 utility library that gives build tools, repository scanners, code generators, documentation tools, validators, and indexers a common API for detecting and describing conventional project directories. It recognizes Maven, Gradle, JavaScript or TypeScript, and Python projects and supplies a filesystem-based default fallback. Consumers configure a project root, detect the appropriate ProjectLayout, and retrieve project-relative source, test, documentation, and module paths without duplicating ecosystem-specific directory conventions. Maven layouts parse pom.xml metadata, Gradle layouts use the Gradle Tooling API, JavaScript layouts read package.json workspaces, Python layouts identify pyproject.toml projects, and DefaultProjectLayout discovers eligible immediate child directories when no supported descriptor is present.

constructors.description: Creates the minimal fallback ProjectLayout implementation. After projectDir(java.io.File) configures the root, getModules() discovers eligible immediate child directories; source, test, and document roots are empty because this fallback does not infer language-specific folders.

examples.description: Create and configure the fallback layout, then obtain immediate child directories that can be processed as potential modules.

constructors.description: Creates a Maven-aware layout. Configure the project root before querying module declarations and Maven source, resource, test, or documentation roots.

examples.description: Configure a Maven project root and retrieve production roots for a scanner or generator.

features.name: detectProjectLayout
features.signature: public static org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout detectProjectLayout(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.FileNotFoundException
features.description: Detects a Maven, Gradle, JavaScript or TypeScript, or Python layout for the supplied project directory and configures it with that directory. When no supported descriptor is found, it returns DefaultProjectLayout.

examples.description: Use automatic detection when one tool must process repositories from multiple build ecosystems.

features.name: getModules
features.description: Returns child module paths for a configured layout. Maven reads pom.xml module declarations, Gradle reads child projects, JavaScript expands workspace globs, and DefaultProjectLayout uses immediate eligible subdirectories. A flat project can return null.

examples.description: Enumerate modules safely before recursively analyzing each module directory.

features.name: getSources
features.description: Returns production source roots relative to the configured project root. Implementations provide ecosystem-specific conventions or metadata-derived paths.

examples.description: Resolve returned relative paths against the configured root before scanning source files.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout
studs.description: Common contract for configured project layouts, defining project-relative discovery of source, test, and documentation roots together with shared path utilities.

examples.description: Program against the common abstraction so tooling works with all supported project ecosystems.

examples.name: Install, configure, and use Project Layout from a Maven application
steps: Install the library by adding the Maven dependency shown in dependencyConfiguration to the consuming application's pom.xml.
For this snapshot version, configure a repository that publishes the snapshot or build and install the artifact locally with mvn install from this project root.
Create a java.io.File for the repository to analyze and call org.machanism.machai.project.ProjectLayoutManager.detectProjectLayout.
Invoke the consuming application with its target repository path; it can use getSources(), getTests(), getDocuments(), and getModules() to drive processing.
examples.description: Build and install Project Layout into the local Maven repository, configure the dependency in a consuming application, and invoke that application with a repository path. The example class name represents the consumer entry point that wraps ProjectLayoutManager.

examples.name: Process a Maven multi-module repository
steps: Pass the parent directory containing pom.xml to the layout manager.
Get module paths from the detected layout and check for null because flat projects may not declare modules.
Resolve each module against the parent directory and detect its layout before processing its source roots.
examples.description: This scenario lets an indexer or generator traverse Maven modules without hard-coding source-directory conventions.
